sentences.text: Opposite Party :- State Of U.P. Thru. Addl. Chief Secy. Deptt. Of Home Lko.
And 3 Others
Counsel for Applicant :- Anand Kumar Srivastava,Vivek Kumar Srivastava

Counsel for Opposite Party :- G.A.
Hon'ble Pankaj Bhatia,J.
1.
Heard learned counsel for the applicant as well as learned A.G.A. and perused the record.
Despite service of notice, no one appeared on behalf of the complainant.

2. The applicant seeks enlargement on bail in FIR No.30 of 2022, under Sections 363, 366-A, 344,
323, 376 IPC and Section 3/4 of POCSO Act, Police Station Harraiya, District Balrampur.
3. Initially a missing person report was lodged.
Subsequently, in the statement under Section 161 of Cr.P.C., the victim stated that the applicant had taken her to Lucknow and they stayed for 17 days.
The allegation of rape was made in the statement under Section 161 of Cr.P.C.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: under Section 164 of Cr.P.C., she stated that she knew the applicant for the last three months.
She also alleged that some sweet was administered and as a result whereof, she claimed to be under the hands of the applicant for a period of 10 days.
She admitted that she was going with the applicant at Lucknow.
Although the allegation of rape was made, the victim denied to undergo medical examination as is clear from Annexure-4 to the bail application.
There is no document with regard to the age on record, however, the age of the victim has been certified by the CMO at around 16.5 years.

4. In the light of the aforesaid, the Counsel for the applicant argues that admittedly the victim stayed with the applicant for a period of 16 days at Lucknow, during which, she did not raise any alarm.
He further argues that there is no documents with regard to the age of the victim in terms of the mandate of Juvenile Justice Act and the Rules framed thereunder.
5. Learned A.G.A. vehemently opposed the bail prayer.

6. Considering the statements under Sections 161 and 164 of Cr.P.C. and the fact that the victim had refused to undergo medical examination coupled with the fact that the applicant has no criminal antecedents and is in custody since 25.02.2022 and there is nothing on record to demonstrate that the applicant if enlarged on bail, would in any way adversely affect the trial, I am of the view that the applicant is entitled to be released on bail.
Accordingly, the bail application is allowed.

7. Let the applicant Chhotu @ Karamjeet be released on bail in the aforesaid first information report on his furnishing personal bonds and two reliable sureties of the like amount each to the satisfaction of the court concerned with the following conditions:
(a) The applicant shall execute a bond to undertake to attend the hearings;
(b) The applicant shall not commit any offence similar to the offence of which he is accused or suspected of the commission; and (c) The applicant shall not directly or indirectly make any inducement, threat or promise to any person acquainted with the facts of the case so as to dissuade him from disclosing such facts to the Court or to any police officer or tamper with the evidence.
